title: Hacker Runs Hermes AI Agent Unattended for Post-Exploitation at Thai Finance Ministry

reading.body:
An autonomous AI agent called Hermes was deployed by an attacker against Thailand's Ministry of Finance in July 2026 to automate post-exploitation activities after initial network access was gained. The agent ran unattended and performed network enumeration, attempted access to mail systems and Hadoop infrastructure, and conducted privilege escalation testing. This represents a failure in network segmentation and access controls, where an intruder was able to establish persistent footholds across multiple government systems.

The attack required no detection or human intervention to execute the automated tasks. The operator installed a custom implant called Hades and used hardcoded credentials to target various ministry services. Whether sensitive files were actually stolen is not established in the reporting. Catching this attack would have required monitoring for unusual network enumeration activity, restricting service accounts from accessing multiple systems simultaneously, and detecting the implant deployment before the automated agent ran.

The use of AI automation in this attack shows how attackers can scale reconnaissance and exploitation activities once they gain initial access. The ministry's systems did not restrict an AI agent's ability to move laterally or test vulnerabilities across multiple services. No confirmation exists of the attacker's intent or the full scope of compromised data, only of the tools deployed and the systems targeted.

summary:
# Summary

Thailand's Ministry of Finance was targeted by attackers using an autonomous AI agent called Hermes between early and mid-July 2026. Researchers discovered three exposed directories on a Hong Kong server containing exploit code, malicious scripts, and stolen credentials. The operator deployed a custom implant called Hades and ran the AI agent in unattended mode to enumerate the ministry's network, access mail systems, and attempt to compromise Hadoop infrastructure and other internal services. The attack affected multiple government systems including administrative panels and data platforms.

Authorities were notified on July 15, 2026, after the researchers identified the breach. The attackers used hardcoded credentials targeting various ministry services and staged multiple known vulnerabilities for Windows and Linux systems. Evidence suggests the operator was Chinese-speaking and used infrastructure across Hong Kong and Malaysia. While the researchers found logs showing the AI agent conducted privilege escalation testing and network enumeration, there is no confirmation that sensitive files were stolen from the ministry's servers.
